name: Mayal Lyang Homestay
summary: A long-running Lepcha family homestay in Lingthem, upper Dzongu, named after the Lepcha word for their homeland. Simple rooms, three home-cooked Lepcha meals a day, help with the Dzongu permit and local guides for village and waterfall walks.
body: Mayal Lyang is one of the homestays that helped put Dzongu on the map for independent travellers. It is run by a Lepcha family in Lingthem village, on the slopes above the Teesta in upper Dzongu. The name comes from Mayel Lyang, the Lepcha name for their homeland, which says a lot about how the family frames the stay: you are a guest in a Lepcha home, not a hotel.

Expect simple, clean rooms, home-cooked Lepcha and Nepali food from the family kitchen, and evenings around the fire. The family can help arrange the Dzongu permit, pickups from Mangan, and guides for walks to villages, cardamom groves, waterfalls and, when access allows, Tholung Monastery. Rates, room types and the road situation change; confirm all of them directly when you book, and check current status before you travel.
why: A real Lepcha family home in the heart of the Dzongu reserve
Help with the Dzongu permit, transport and local guides
Lepcha home food, including nettle soup, ferns and chi

faqs.a: In Lingthem village, upper Dzongu, North Sikkim, across the Teesta from Mangan. It is reached by taxi from Mangan after you collect your Dzongu permit, roughly 1–1.5 hours depending on the road. The family can usually arrange a pickup.

faqs.q: Does Mayal Lyang help with the Dzongu permit?
faqs.a: Dzongu homestays, including Mayal Lyang, commonly help guests arrange the Dzongu permit by guiding them through the paperwork or applying in advance with your ID copies. Ask when you book what they need and how long it takes. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does Mayal Lyang cost?
faqs.a: Expect roughly ₹1,800–2,500 per person per day with all meals in 2025–26, but this is indicative. Guides and transport are extra. Confirm the current rate and what it includes directly with the family before you travel.

name: Yarlam Resort
summary: One of the better-known hotels in Lachung, on the edge of the village with views up the valley. It costs more than the homestays, and suits couples and families who want heated rooms and a dependable base for Yumthang and Zero Point.
body: Most Lachung rooms are in small family hotels and homestays assigned by tour operators. Yarlam Resort is one of the established, larger properties that travellers book by name, usually for a Comfort-tier trip or a honeymoon. It sits on the edge of the village with mountain views, and it is used to tour-group schedules: early breakfasts for Yumthang and late dinners after the long drive.

We list it because it is well known and has operated for years, not because we have inspected every room. It is a step up in price from homestays, so book it if a warm room and more reliable hot water matter to you in winter. Confirm heating, hot water, meal plans and current rates when you book, and check current status of the North Sikkim road before you travel.
why: An established Lachung hotel used to tour schedules
A warmer, more comfortable option for winter and honeymoons
Easy base for the 6 am Yumthang and Zero Point departure

faqs.q: Is Yarlam Resort a good place to stay in Lachung?
faqs.a: It is one of the better-known hotels in Lachung and a good choice if you want more comfort than a homestay, especially in winter. It costs more than village homestays. Confirm room type, heating and meals when booking, through your agent or the hotel directly.

faqs.q: Can I book Yarlam Resort on a shared tour?
faqs.a: Shared tours usually assign standard hotels or homestays. Some Gangtok agents will upgrade you to a named hotel such as Yarlam for an extra charge. Ask your agent for the difference in price per person before you pay.

faqs.q: How far is Yarlam Resort from Yumthang?
faqs.a: Yarlam is in Lachung, about 24 km and an hour's drive below Yumthang Valley. Tours collect guests early in the morning for Yumthang and, if booked, Zero Point. Breakfast timing is usually arranged around the departure.

name: Singhik Tourist Lodge
summary: A Sikkim Tourism lodge on the Singhik ridge, 4 km above Mangan, chosen for its view across the Teesta gorge to Kanchenjunga and Siniolchu. Simple rooms, a calm first night on the way north, and a sunrise view a few steps from the door.
body: Government tourist lodges were built in Sikkim's viewpoint villages to give travellers a dependable bed at a fair price, and the one at Singhik was placed for the view. From its terrace and west-facing rooms you look over the deep Teesta valley to the Kanchenjunga massif and Siniolchu. On clear mornings from October to April, that alone justifies the night.

Rooms are simple, and service follows government-lodge standards rather than hotel ones. Use it as a quiet first night on a North Sikkim trip, splitting the long drive to Lachung or Lachen, or as a base for Mangan and Dzongu. We have not been able to confirm current booking channels and rates, so contact Sikkim Tourism or a Gangtok agent before you travel and check that the lodge is operating.
why: West-facing view of Kanchenjunga and Siniolchu at sunrise
A cheaper, gentler first night than going straight to Lachung
Close to Mangan for Dzongu permits and shared jeeps

faqs.q: How do I book the Singhik Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Through Sikkim Tourism or a Gangtok travel agent. Booking channels change, so call or ask an agent before you travel and confirm that the lodge is operating. In October and April, book a few weeks ahead for a view room.

faqs.q: Does the Singhik lodge have a Kanchenjunga view?
faqs.a: Yes, that is its main attraction. The lodge looks west across the Teesta gorge to the Kanchenjunga massif and Siniolchu. Views are clearest at sunrise from October to April; cloud often hides the peaks later in the day and in the monsoon.

faqs.q: Is Singhik Tourist Lodge good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. It is quiet, at a mild altitude of about 1,560 m, and breaks the long drive north into two easier days. Rooms are simple. Bring warm layers for winter nights and confirm meals when you book.
